courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Systems design third-year students will meet with a faculty member designated as their class professor. Performance in assignments, conceptual difficulties with courses, interrelation of coursework, later work and engineering practice will be discussed.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Systems design third-year students will meet with a faculty member designated as their class professor. Performance in assignments, conceptual difficulties with courses, interrelation of coursework, later work and engineering practice will be discussed.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Advanced Engineering Math 2
courses.description: Series solutions of ordinary differential equations; Bessel functions, orthogonal functions, Fourier expansions and integral, Legendre polynomials, Sturm-Liouville systems. Partial differential equations; parabolic, hyperbolic and elliptic equations, numerical methods. Numerical integration; Gaussian quadrature, Runge-Kutta methods. Nonlinear systems; qualitative analysis, phase plane, Newton-Raphson method.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Applied Linear Algebra
courses.description: Vector spaces, linear independence, linear maps and matrix representations. Inner product spaces and orthogonality. Gramm-Schmidt algorithm and orthogonal projection. Interpolation and curve-fitting. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, singular value decomposition. Applications and numerical methods.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Introduction to Responsible Artificial Intelligence Systems
courses.description: The objective of this course is to introduce students to fundamental concepts of artificial intelligence. An overview of different learning schemes will be provided, including supervised and unsupervised algorithms. The course will review some data science methods (dimensionality reduction, clustering, classification, Markov decision processes). The focus will be on the development of deep and shallow neural networks and their application in solving engineering problems, which also includes data curation and training procedures. The context of the course will be on the responsible development and deployment of AI systems, including their limitations, risk minimization and management, ethical considerations, reliability, robustness, scalability, and sustainability.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Software Design
courses.description: Software requirements specification; software architecture; design patterns; software testing and quality assurance; software maintenance; design of efficient algorithms and methods for their analysis, mathematical algorithms, string processing algorithms, geometrical algorithms, exhaustive search and traversal techniques, introduction to lower bound theory and NP-completeness. Case studies and engineering examples.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Applied Statistics
courses.description: Review of basic Normal theory, t, chi-squared, and F distributions. Simple linear regression. Lack of fit. Analysis of variance. Multiple linear regression, variable selection techniques, indicator variables, diagnostics. Brief introduction to non-linear regression, factorial experimentation.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Systems Models 1
courses.description: Introduction to systems modelling and analysis. Graph theoretic models and formulation of system equations. State space formulation and solution. Time and frequency domain solutions. Application to engineering systems.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Introduction to Control Systems
courses.description: Classical and state space representations of control systems. Stability, controllability, observability and sensitivity. Routh-Hurwitz and root-locus methods. Frequency domain behaviour, Bode plots, Nyquist stability criteria. Pole placement, PID, phase-lead and phase-lag controllers.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Control Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory experiments for students taking SYDE352.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Systems Design Methods 1: Needs Analysis and Prototyping
courses.description: The methodology of design, situation of concern; needs analysis and problem definition, engineering analysis and generation of alternative solutions, design prototyping, and design documentation. The lecture material is supplemented by a term-long design project done in small groups that develops hands-on experience with electromechanical prototyping.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Design Testing, Validation, and Verification
courses.description: Engineering design project course where students work in small groups applying the principles of engineering problem solving and design, with a focus on testing and design evaluation, and an introduction to benchmark testing and applied design optimization. Student projects will provide hands-on experience with design verification, validation, and performance measurement and analysis using engineering tools.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Design Consultation
courses.description: In this course, students will engage with stakeholders, colleagues, communities, and the natural world as they apply human-centered and participatory design practices to fully understand a complex design problem in its broader societal and environmental context. Students will develop and represent a deep understanding of the design problem while acknowledging their own knowledge gaps, deficiencies in existing solutions, and uncertainties. Students will work with each other and stakeholders to determine viable solution approaches while considering a wide range of options including new or changes to existing products, processes, infrastructure, policy, or other systems.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: An introductory course in engineering thermodynamics structured for students in systems design. Classical thermodynamics is presented as the systematic study of energy; its use, degradation, and waste. Introduction to heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation. Applications focus on problems of energy and environment. The concepts of statistical thermodynamics are introduced.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Multi-Physics Modelling and Simulation
courses.description: Introduction to describing physical phenomena in differential form such as fluid flow (Navier-Stokes), thermodynamics (energy conservation, enthalpy, entropy), electro-magnetics (Maxwell equations), mechanics, and dynamics.  Topics include finite difference methods, finite element methods, boundary conditions, and iterative solvers.  The objective is to model with differential equations, predict what the result characteristics, solve models with FEM computational algorithms, and authenticate the results.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Fundamental concepts in systems involving fluid flow. Basic treatment of statics, kinematics and dynamics of fluids. Conservation of mass, momentum and energy for a control volume. Dimensional analysis and similarity. Flow in pipes and channels. Brief introduction to boundary layers, lift and drag, ideal and compressible flow.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Material Properties
courses.description: An introduction to the properties, processing and structure of metals, semiconductors, polymers, ceramic, nanomaterials, and biomaterials. Introduction to mechanical response of materials and stress-strain relationships. Behaviour of prismatic members in tension, compression, shear, bending, and torsion. Shear-force and bending-moment diagrams and an introduction to instability.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Work-Term Symposium Presentation
courses.description: A work-term presentation is composed and presented at the Work-term Symposium. The presentation provides an opportunity for students to effectively communicate and reflect on their engineering experience gained during their co-op work terms. In the presentation, students draw connections between the theoretical aspects of engineering taught in the classroom and the practical applications of that theory in the workplace.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Systems design fourth-year students will meet with a faculty member designated as their class professor. Conceptual difficulties, the interrelation of course work and engineering practice will be discussed.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Systems design fourth-year students will meet with a faculty member designated as their class professor. Conceptual difficulties, the interrelation of course work and engineering practice will be discussed.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Optimization and Numerical Methods
courses.description: Advanced methods for systems of linear equations. Root-finding methods. Linear programming, simplex and interior-point methods. Local and global optimization methods. Constrained optimization. Multiobjective and multidisciplinary design optimization.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Systems Design Engineering Capstone Project 1
courses.description: The first half of a two-term engineering design project continuing the systems design project sequence. Students work in small groups applying the principles of systems design engineering to a situation of concern of their own choosing. Students have individual project supervisors as well as an overall co-ordinator who provides the framework for the term assessments.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Systems Design Engineering Capstone Project 2
courses.description: The second half of a two-term engineering design project continuing the systems design project sequence. Students work in small groups applying the principles of systems design engineering to a situation of concern of their own choosing. Students have individual project supervisors as well as an overall co-ordinator who provides the framework for the term assessments.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Elective Systems Design Research Project
courses.description: A major undergraduate individual systems design engineering research project carried out as a technical elective (TE) under the supervision of a faculty member. Students are expected to demonstrate initiative and responsibility. An oral presentation of results and a written report are the minimum requirements. The faculty supervisor or department may set other requirements. Students will arrange for a faculty supervisor prior to registration.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: The objective of this course is to introduce students to fundamental concepts of artificial intelligence. An overview of different learning schemes will be provided, including supervised and unsupervised algorithms. The focus of this course will be on dimensionality reduction, clustering, classification, deep and shallow artificial neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Ethical aspects of artificial intelligence will be discussed.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Design Optimization Under Probabilistic Uncertainty
courses.description: Optimization methods for real world problems have to deal with probabilistic uncertainty either due to data uncertainty or manufacturing uncertainty or both. Maximizing the expected value of the objective function subject to reliability (or risk) constraints is commonly used in such design or decision-making problems. Common methods used are stochastic programming, stochastic dynamic programming, chance-constraints, yield optimization and tolerance design. Example applications are selected from water management, energy systems, financial engineering, and manufacturing.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Introduction to Complex Systems
courses.description: The overwhelming majority of societal, ecological and climate issues of pressing importance are complex systems; nonlinear dynamic interacting systems poorly characterized by linear analyses and Gaussian statistics. This course introduces the mathematics needed to understand such interactions, including nonlinear dynamics, critical and bifurcation behaviours, large-scale systems and power-law distributions. The mathematical methods will be motivated by extensive examples and case studies such as global warming, energy shortages, desertification, overpopulation, poverty, and economic instability, to be investigated from a systems engineering perspective that will connect mathematical concepts to real-world examples.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Conflict Resolution
courses.description: Formal methods for studying engineering decision-making problems involving multiple participants and multiple objectives. Topics include the graph model for conflict resolution, normal game form, metagame analysis, games with misperceptions, preference elicitation, human behaviour under conflict, evolution of a conflict, decision-making under uncertainty, sensitivity analyses, multiple criteria decision analysis, group decision and negotiation, coalition analysis, decision support systems, and real-world applications of the foregoing concepts.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Electric Energy Systems
courses.description: Traditional electric energy systems comprising generation, transmission, and distribution are examined. Emerging technologies and trends are considered, such as competition, smart grids, energy storage, demand side management, renewable energy, and P2P. Future challenges and possibilities are then explored. Issues will be explored from technical, economic, environmental, sustainability, and social perspectives.
antireqText: Not completed nor concurrently enrolled in: SYDE599 (Topic 10: Electric Energy Systems)

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Computational Simulations for Societal and Environmental Systems
courses.description: This course will introduce and apply the fundamentals of computational simulation for complex systems. Data collection and analysis, conceptual modelling, computational modelling, output analysis, and communication of results to non-expert audiences will be covered extensively. Students will develop computational simulations to explore potential solutions for complex societal problems, identifying emergent scenarios, costs, and benefits with the goal of informing decision-makers.
antireqText: Not completed nor concurrently enrolled in: SYDE599 (Topic 9: Computational Simulations for Societal and Environmental Systems)

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Modelling Transportation Systems
courses.description: Overview of frameworks used to model the global and community transportation systems followed by four case studies: Bayesian modelling of collision rates; discrete choice modelling of travel mode; operating mode-based time series modelling of tailpipe emissions, and simulation of traffic operations including congestion.
antireqText: Not completed nor concurrently enrolled in: SYDE599 (Topic 7: Transportation Modelling)

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Artificial Life: Biology and Computation
courses.description: Artificial life is the study of the simulation and synthesis of living or life-like systems. This course treats the basic principles of biology and computation in nature that underpin the organization of living systems in life as we know it, as it might exist elsewhere in the universe, and in digital or artificial media. We explore the mechanisms within living individuals that grow and change in a complex environment. This provides a variety of methods for understanding, modelling, and designing complex adaptive systems, whether naturally occurring or engineered, in simulation, in physical systems, with a view to applications in artificial life as the foundation for artificial intelligence and biological modelling.
antireqText: Not completed nor concurrently enrolled in: SYDE599 (Topic 3: Biology and Computation)

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Interface Design
courses.description: This course focuses on the design of computer interfaces for simple to complex systems. Examples of applications are used to illustrate theoretical approaches. Main topics include forms of visual display; auditory display and soft controls; context, navigation, and layout; development techniques; design for engagement.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Cognitive Ergonomics
courses.description: This course focuses on the role engineering psychology research plays in design of the information displays and devices associated with simple and complex cognitive tasks. Main topics include signal detection and target location tasks, navigation tasks, training tasks, communication tasks, human error, stress and mental workload, supervisory control, and situational awareness.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Biomedical Measurement and Signal Processing
courses.description: This course develops an understanding of biomedical measurements through the examination of electromyographic (EMG), electroencephalographic (EEG), and electrocardiographic (ECG) signals. Measurement of human-body position, force, and pressure, and related instrumentation will also be presented. Signal processing techniques will be discussed in the context of extraction and application of useful biomedical signals.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: User Centred Design Methods
courses.description: This course approaches the design of tasks, tools, products, and systems from a user-centered design perspective. Emphasis is on the human factors and usability methods, and techniques that can and should be applied throughout the iterative design process. While design issues pertaining to human-computer interaction are discussed, the methods presented can be applied to the design of almost any user interface. Major topics include user research methods for usability and user experience, inspection methods, user testing, applied statistical analysis.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Computational Neuroscience
courses.description: Introduction to modelling and analysis of neurophysiological systems. Models of synaptic plasticity and learning, with focus on the similarities and differences between neuroscience and deep learning.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Advanced Dynamics
courses.description: Newtonian and Eulerian formulation of particle and rigid body kinematics and dynamics. Energy (Lagrangian and Hamiltonian) formulations of particle and rigid body dynamics; generalized co-ordinates, generalized forces, holonomic constraints, Lagrange multipliers.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Nonlinear Dynamic Systems
courses.description: This course introduces nonlinear systems with applications in realistic ecological, mechanical, electrical, and chemical engineering systems. The properties of those systems are investigated via analytical and numerical tools, with particular application to MEMS and NEMS actuators & sensors. Students will develop knowledge and appreciation of the following concepts and tools: differences between linear and nonlinear dynamic systems; autonomous and non-autonomous systems; existence and uniqueness of solutions; equilibrium points and limit cycles; phase plane analysis; nonlinear phenomena; Poincare section analysis; multi-frequency oscillations; notions of system stability (e.g., Lyapunov functions).
antireqText: Not completed nor concurrently enrolled in: SYDE599 (Topic 14: Nonlinear Dynamic Systems)

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Simulating Neurobiological Systems
courses.description: This course develops and applies a general framework for understanding neural computation in the context of recent advances in theoretical and experimental neuroscience. Particular emphasis is placed on understanding representation, nonlinear computation, and dynamics in real neurobiological systems. Students will apply signal processing, control theory, linear algebra, probability theory, and similar quantitative tools for the purpose of modelling sensory, motor, and cognitive systems. Topics covered include single neuron function, neural coding, neural dynamics, attractor networks, learning, statistical inference, locomotion, working memory, etc. Familiarity with neural systems is helpful but not essential.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Introduction to Pattern Recognition
courses.description: Pattern recognition as a process of data analysis. Pattern features as components in a random vector representation. Classification techniques; distance measures in feature space, probabilistic (Bayesian) decision theory, linear discriminants. Clustering and feature extraction. Applications; optical character recognition, speech recognition, industrial robot vision, medical diagnosis, remote sensing and satellite image analysis, fault detection and diagnosis in complex systems such as nuclear reactors.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Image Processing
courses.description: Beginning with a discussion of quantitative models of imaging systems, this course moves on to apply methods of linear systems theory and signal processing to image processing. Simple spatial domain techniques as well as spatial frequency domain methods, and digital filter design for image enhancement and restoration are discussed. The key methods and problems are surveyed; edge detection, image denoising, image segmentation, image enhancement, image compression, image registration, and feature detection. Applications to machine vision, remote sensing, and medical imaging will be emphasized.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Deep Learning
courses.description: Introduction to deep learning. Regression and classification; backpropagation; convolutional and recurrent networks; optimization and regularization of deep networks; transformers; recent developments in the field.
antireqText: Not completed nor concurrently enrolled in: SYDE599 (Topic 4: Deep Learning)

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Physiological Systems and Biomedical Design
courses.description: In this course, students will become familiar with the physiology and anatomical structures of the human body. The structure, functions, and properties of major physiological systems (e.g., musculoskeletal, nervous, cardiovascular, and respiratory) will be presented in relation to modelling physiological systems and the design of biomedical devices (imaging, assistive, and diagnostic). Various aspects of pathology and how they influence measurements will also be introduced.

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Material Selection for Design
courses.description: Material selection based on material property and design requirements. Design a product and selected material against failure. Select a manufacturing process that meets design requirements and constraints. Incorporate economic analysis and environmental impact in the selection process. Assess life cycle of the product and the selected material. Case studies related to general engineering applications and biomedical applications.
antireqText: Not completed nor concurrently enrolled in: SYDE599 (Topic 2: Material Selection for Design)

courses.subject: SYDE
courses.title: Special Topics in Systems Design Engineering
courses.description: This course deals with selected topics at the undergraduate level in environmental and societal systems, mechatronics and physical systems, or human factors and ergonomics.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Introduction to Theatre
courses.description: A foundational studio course introducing students to the technical dimensions of theatre creation with emphasis on design and production processes. Students explore the material elements that bring performance to life through hands-on engagement with production technologies, design principles, and technical problem-solving. Through studio-based workshops and collaborative projects, students develop introductory skills in scenic construction, lighting, sound, costumes, and props while examining how these technical elements express genre, style, theme, and narrative structure. Students research and analyze influential dramatic works and develop original production designs that address contemporary issues such as race, gender, and sustainability. This required course establishes essential technical vocabulary, conceptual frameworks, and practical skills needed for both acting and production streams, with particular emphasis on how technical choices impact storytelling and audience experience.
courses.notes: • Prior experience in theatre-making is not required.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Theatre and Performance Fundamentals
courses.description: This foundational course introduces students to theatre through three integrated pillars: dramaturgy (historical context, critical investigation, theory), performance (acting techniques, creation, embodiment), and production and design (stagecraft and scenography). Designed for both theatre majors seeking essential foundations and students from all disciplines, the course develops critical thinking, artistic research practices, creative problem-solving, and collaborative abilities applicable across fields.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Introduction to Performance
courses.description: A foundational studio course introducing students to the creative processes of performance across a range of contexts. Students develop core performance skills through embodied practice, collaborative creation, and critical reflection. The course emphasizes physical awareness, vocal expressivity, textual analysis, and ensemble building while exploring the relationship between performance and identity. Through progressive exercises, improvisation, scene work, and performance projects, students cultivate presence, authenticity, and creative risk-taking. This required course serves as the entry point to further specialization, establishing the groundwork for understanding performance as a mode of meaning-making and social engagement.
courses.notes: • Prior performance experience is not required.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Introduction to Black Arts, Culture, and Literature
courses.description: This course examines the evolution and development of Black Peoples' artistic, cultural, and literary experiences from a global perspective including art and design, theatre and performance, literature, music, spoken word, and other modes of interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary practice. Coursework is designed to immerse students in analyzing Black art, culture, and literature through intersectional, feminist, and queer lenses. The course is designed for both thinkers and creators. Students will engage in the course material through readings, viewings, and field trips around film, comics, anime, popular culture events, plus the visual and performing arts.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Introduction to Critical Design Practices
courses.description: How does design help us think? This studio course introduces students to practice-based methods for generating knowledge. Topics may include prototyping, performance as research, material thinking, multi-modal representation, and experience design. Students will test and explore how we learn differently through creative practices.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Performance Studies
courses.description: This workshop course in performance studies explores performance as a way of knowing. It investigates performance as artistic practice and as a means of understanding historical, social, and cultural practices, including drama/theatre texts, poetry, narratives, and texts of everyday life.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Performing Text
courses.description: Students explore techniques to analyze, interpret, and perform texts.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Intermediate Performance
courses.description: Building upon foundations from THPERF100 and COMMST102/THPERF102, this studio course advances students' performance skills through increasingly challenging material and expanded creative exploration. Students deepen their physical and vocal expressivity while engaging with diverse acting approaches and performance styles that complexify their understanding of character development and textual interpretation. Through scene study, ensemble exercises, and collaborative projects, students cultivate artistic confidence and discover their individual creative voice. The course emphasizes the development of versatile performers who can navigate multiple performance contexts while beginning to identify their artistic interests and pathways toward advanced specialization.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Black Performance Studies
courses.description: This course explores the genealogies and historical development of Black performance created in regions such as North America, the Caribbean, Africa, and Europe. Students will examine the influences of key artists and theorists. Students will be challenged to apply historical, political, and cultural contexts to the analysis of audio, text-based, and/or audio-visual materials. This course expands students' concepts of Black performance to include performative modes such as performance poetry, TV shows, music, and podcasts.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Staging Science: Embodying Knowledge Expression in the Sciences
courses.description: This course explores the vital intersections between science and theatre, from the anatomical theatres of the 1700s to the rigour of laboratory experimentation to contemporary high-stakes science communication. Students develop practical, collaborative, and embodied performance skills while investigating how theatrical processes shape scientific knowledge production and public understanding. Object texts may include plays, genres of science writing, and performance theory. Through staging and assembling performances, students experiment with how media - materials, bodies, technologies, and spatial relationships - matter for making and expressing knowledge, ultimately cultivating dramaturgical approaches that bridge scientific and artistic modes of inquiry.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Introduction to Modern Arab and Muslim Drama
courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of modern Arab and Muslim drama, providing students with a deep understanding of its various contexts, genres, evolutions, themes, and aesthetic nuances. Moreover, students will actively engage in the transformative practice of Theatre of the Oppressed, where they will merge their creative skills with scholarly knowledge. Collaborating in groups, they will create and perform Forum plays that serve as reflections on pertinent socio-political issues explored in the course. This blend of theoretical exploration and practical application ensures a holistic and immersive learning experience, fostering critical thinking, empathy, and artistic expression.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Technical Production 1
courses.description: This course offers Theatre and Performance students an opportunity to contribute as crew members on mainstage productions within the school, working within a specific technical area to realize the scenic, lighting, costume, sound, and projection elements that audiences will experience. Through extensive hands-on practice in wardrobe, carpentry, scenic painting, lighting, sound, and video projection, students integrate theoretical knowledge with the practical demands of live performance. The course requires a significant time commitment as students participate in design meetings, technical rehearsals, and fabrication sessions where they build and install elements for performance. All coursework is completed in person with minimal take-home assignments.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Technical Production 2
courses.description: Building on THPERF243, this course deepens students' technical theatre skills through more advanced crew work on mainstage productions within the school. Students advance their practical expertise within their chosen technical area while taking on increased responsibility in the production process. Through ongoing participation in design meetings, technical rehearsals, and fabrication sessions, students refine their skills and develop greater independence in realizing performance elements. All coursework is completed in person with minimal take-home assignments.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Fundamentals of Design
courses.description: This studio course provides a foundational introduction to the elements and processes of performance design. Students explore the fundamental principles of scenic, lighting, costume, sound, and projection design through hands-on projects and critical analysis. Emphasis is placed on developing visual literacy, understanding the elements of design and principles of composition, and learning scenographic thinking as a means of understanding performance creation across theatre, dance, opera, and performance art.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Project Management in the Arts
courses.description: This course introduces students to principles of project management relevant in a broad range of contexts including theatre, dance, film, and digital media production. Students explore arts management concepts such as budgeting, communication, scheduling, leadership, problem-solving, and conflict resolution. Concepts are applied in case studies that accommodate individual student interests.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Performance History
courses.description: This course offers a broad exploration of theatre and performance practices across time and cultures, examining the evolution of major genres, styles, and traditions with contextual emphasis on Western theatrical developments. From ancient rituals to contemporary expressions, students will investigate how diverse performance forms emerge from and respond to their historical, social, and cultural environments. The course balances the study of significant theatrical movements, texts, and artists with critical approaches to historical research and interpretation. By engaging with influential works and scholarly perspectives, students will develop a nuanced understanding of how performance has been created, documented, and reimagined throughout history, while considering the complex relationship between theatrical traditions and the societies that produce them.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: THPERF371

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Gender and Performance
courses.description: This course explores how gender is performed on the stage and in the media. Key performances and performers are studied from the perspectives of critical feminist theory and performance studies. Students consider how performances can create, affirm, and disrupt how society understands and performs gender.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Special Topics in Theatre and Performance
courses.description: Selected topics in theatre and performance at the introductory and intermediate level. Content varies based on faculty expertise, visiting artists, and student interest. Topics may include emerging trends in performance creation, specialized design techniques, contemporary theatre practices, theatre and performance studies, or interdisciplinary approaches to theatrical work.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Performance Creation
courses.description: An integrated course exploring diverse approaches to creating original performance across multiple contexts and media. Students study, apply, and critique a range of collaborative creation methodologies, with special attention to site-specific performance and place-making through the body, language, space, and technology. The course emphasizes the relationship between creative processes and the significance of works in their communities, examining how performance can respond to, challenge, and transform social contexts. Through hands-on projects, students develop skills in collaborative leadership, interdisciplinary research, and critical analysis of artistic processes.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Production and Performance Practicum
courses.description: This intermediate-level practicum course engages students in predominantly hands-on theatrical practice across performance, design, and production specializations through substantial leadership roles in the program's theatre productions. Building upon foundational coursework, students work alongside faculty, staff, and visiting artists to develop professional-level competencies in industry-standard practices. Across multiple practicum enrolments, students may explore different aspects of theatre creation, including performance, acting, directing, design, technical stagecraft, management, dramaturgy, and publicity, with each production offering distinct content and specialized focus areas that bridge academic learning with professional theatrical work.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Approaches to Acting with Text
courses.description: Students apply conceptual and theoretical approaches to acting in traditions emphasizing the text as a resource for performance.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Advanced Performance
courses.description: This intensive studio course challenges students with complex technique development and creative exploration through demanding classical and contemporary material. Students refine advanced physical and vocal skills while tackling challenging texts that require artistic maturity and technical precision. The course emphasizes integration of multiple performance approaches as students develop their distinctive artistic voice through advanced scene study, physical theatre techniques, and collaborative devising processes. Students push artistic boundaries through challenging solo and ensemble work that explores the full range of their developing abilities.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Performing the Voice
courses.description: Students explore techniques to access and develop the voice as a resource for performance.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Stage Management
courses.description: Students explore approaches to stage management for theatre and performance.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Intermediate Design
courses.description: Building on design fundamentals, this intermediate studio course engages students in collaborative, project-based design practice. Students work independently and as a team to develop complete design concepts for theatre and performance works and integrated digital media projects that draw upon contemporary scenographic methods. The course emphasizes professional design processes, research methodologies, and the creation of design presentations for real-world production contexts. Students explore how design intersects with social issues and contemporary performance practices.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Approaches to Directing
courses.description: Exploration of the director's task in its practical, theoretical, and historical aspects.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Shakespeare in Performance at the Stratford Festival
courses.description: A historical, theoretical, and analytical introduction to Shakespeare's plays in performance, both on stage and screen, this course focuses on specific problems and decisive issues of past productions and of those in the current Stratford Festival season.
courses.notes: • The course is offered as part of a consortium with faculty from five universities. • Students are required to arrange their own transportation to Stratford.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Writing for Performance
courses.description: Students explore techniques for analyzing, interpreting, and creating texts for theatre and performance.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Voice and Text at the Stratford Festival
courses.description: Taught by faculty and Stratford Festival coaches, this practical course invites students to explore acting techniques and exercises to develop their stage voice with a particular focus on Shakespeare's plays. This is a block course that meets in Stratford for two weeks in May, and may be taken with ENGL364/THPERF364, as the two courses are offered at complementary times.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Sustainability in Design
courses.description: Students explore the interchange between performance design and sustainability. Emphasis will be placed on ecological and systems thinking as students engage with theoretical and practical projects throughout the term.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Political Performance
courses.description: This course offers a practical and applied examination of how various forms of performance may bring about an experience of political conscientization because creating a performance can be considered a process of political enlightenment and engagement.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Indigenous Performance in Context
courses.description: This course introduces students to the knowledge systems and performance history woven into the practices of First Peoples on Turtle Island and beyond. Through examination of performance genres ranging from Longhouse, Renewal, and Powwow ceremonies to Western theatre, pop music, and Wild West shows, students will gain understanding of the current Indigenous performance landscape through discussion and critique of design and production history as well as contemporary script analysis. This course engages students in Indigenous Ways of Knowing and helps them develop alternative approaches to research with particular attention to sustainable and holistic practices of performance making and design presentation. The class content will pay particular attention to traditions of the host nations (Haudenosaunee and Anishinaabe) when possible.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Race and Performance
courses.description: This course explores how critical race and performance studies illuminate 20th- and 21st-century theatre and performance. Students investigate the historical, political, and cultural contexts that inform the creation and presentation of performance works involving race, examining how theatre-making can resist or perpetuate structures of oppression and colonization. Through embodied research practices and critical analysis, students explore how racial concepts find expression through performative communication and scenography. Applying intersectional and decolonial approaches, students develop skills to create equitable, accessible, and anti-oppressive performance experiences while building capacity to communicate effectively across diverse artistic contexts and navigate complex creative territories with care and self-awareness.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Mixed Reality Design
courses.description: This course explores design for material-world experiences that incorporate virtual, augmented, and/or extended reality technologies. Emphasis is placed on the relationships among different modes of perception and how they affect our understanding of the real and the virtual.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Black Theatre in Practice
courses.description: A workshop that explores the history, dramatic literature, and performance of Black theatre artists. Students will explore the relationship of Black theatre to artistic and public life. Special attention may be given to specific issues, periods, locations, and genealogies of Black theatre. Students will create performance pieces.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Shakespeare 1
courses.description: A study of the plays written before 1599-1600, excluding Julius Caesar.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Shakespeare 2
courses.description: A study of the plays written after 1599-1600, including Julius Caesar.

courses.description: Selected topics in theatre and performance at the advanced level. Topics may include emerging trends in performance creation, specialized design techniques, contemporary theatre practices, theatre and performance studies, or interdisciplinary approaches to theatrical work. Content varies based on faculty expertise, visiting artists, and student interest.

courses.subject: THPERF
courses.title: Advanced Production and Performance Practicum
courses.description: This course serves as the culminating experience for Theatre and Performance majors. Students work at an advanced, independent level with faculty, staff, and visiting artists to create and reflect upon a major, collaborative performance project. As core members of the creative team, students engage in all areas of project creation, including research, conception, writing, direction, design, performance, production, stage management, production management, publicity, dramaturgy, critique, and documentation.
courses.notes: • The topic from at least one of the prerequisite courses must align with the topic for this course.

courses.title: Production and Performance Practicum
courses.description: This advanced-level practicum course engages students in predominantly hands-on theatrical practice across performance, design, and production specializations through substantial leadership roles in the program's theatre productions. Building upon intermediate practicum experience, students work alongside faculty, staff, and visiting artists to develop professional-level competencies in industry-standard practices. Across multiple practicum enrolments, students may explore different aspects of theatre creation, including performance, acting, directing, design, technical stagecraft, management, dramaturgy, and publicity, with each production offering distinct content and specialized focus areas that bridge academic learning with professional theatrical work.

courses.title: Performative Inquiry and Practice
courses.description: This course explores how to create, perform, and analyze performance texts, here defined as including drama/theatre texts, poetry, narratives, and the texts of everyday life. Through readings and creative investigation, students will explore the links between the participant, the researcher, the site, and the impulse of inquiry.

courses.description: Seminars in special areas of drama and theatre.

courses.subject: UNIV
courses.title: Strategies and Skills for Academic Success
courses.description: The goal for this course is to help students become successful independent learners. It takes a modelled approach to teaching learning strategies to students who struggle to meet the demands of a university curriculum. In the lectures, students will be taught various learning strategies that they will be able to apply to successfully meet the demands of their other courses. Students will then apply these modelled strategies in their other courses during a weekly application seminar. Students will be expected to demonstrate their understanding of the material through a variety of assignments.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: World Cinema and Visual Culture
courses.description: Introduction to film analysis via national cinemas and their worldwide reception, taking into account the role of new technologies. This course acknowledges not only the importance of multiple languages and cultures on the planet today but also the rapidly growing international contexts, complicated chains of production and distribution, and vastly different cultures of spectatorship.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE102
courses.notes: • All films will be shown with subtitles; no second language expertise is required.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Art History and Visual Culture
courses.description: This course takes a case study approach to examining the role of the art object as a means of communication within the history of visual culture. Particular attention will also be paid to the unique properties of a range of diverse media, both traditional and new.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE101

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Introduction to Black Arts, Culture, and Literature
courses.description: This course examines the evolution and development of Black Peoples' artistic, cultural, and literary experiences from a global perspective including art and design, theatre and performance, literature, music, spoken word, and other modes of interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary practice. Coursework is designed to immerse students in analyzing Black art, culture, and literature through intersectional, feminist, and queer lenses. The course is designed for both thinkers and creators. Students will engage in the course material through readings, viewings, and field trips around film, comics, anime, popular culture events, plus the visual and performing arts.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Visual Studies Across the Discipline
courses.description: Weekly lectures by visiting faculty introduce students to how visual studies are conducted across and between the disciplines. Recognizing the vastness of the global study of visual culture, this course reinforces how, despite the diversity of media analyzed, various disciplines share related approaches and theories.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Global Histories of Art 1500-1800 C.E.
courses.description: This course takes a survey approach to examining the role of the art object as a means of communication within the history of global visual culture. Students will study key examples of art, spanning the 16th to the 19th centuries, and will achieve a thematic comprehension of art’s role in shaping political structures, social mores, cultural discourses, and cosmological beliefs. Particular attention will also be paid to the unique properties of a range of diverse media, both traditional and new.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Art Institutions
courses.description: This course examines the history of art institutions, such as museums, galleries, collections, artist run spaces, and considers their place and meaning in contemporary society. Students will explore the history and future shape of such institutions and examine current practices, issues, and debates surrounding them. Topics to be considered include the politics of the art institutions; history and discourse of collecting and display; history of curatorial practices and the development of exhibitions; art publics; technology and new media; collections and collecting practices; and issues  of artistic freedom and censorship.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Topics in Visual Culture
courses.description: This course will cover different topics in visual culture. The content can change from term to term.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Global Modern Art: 1800-1940
courses.description: A study of the global development of modern art (1800 to 1940). Topics such as primitivism, Impressionism, Cubism, Futurism, abstraction, imperialism, colonialism, artists' reactions to calamitous world events such as World War 1, and various methodologies, including semiotic and Marxist analyses, will be explored.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Global Modernisms: 1940-1970
courses.description: This course introduces students to a thematically, materially, and geographically varied set of art practices which developed across the world from 1940-1970 and are referred to, under different monikers, as high modernism, mid-century modernism, and more recently global modernism. These variants of global art production are explored by analyzing theoretical and aesthetic ideas, as well as art movements and styles such as Socialist Realism, Gutai, Postcolonial Modernism, Cannibalist Aesthetic, Brutalism, Abstract Expressionism, Pop Art, Négritude, Indigenous Modernism, and others.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE209
courses.notes: • Art history course.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Indigenous Visual Culture in Canada
courses.description: This course will introduce students to issues in contemporary Indigenous visual culture within the Canadian context. Special attention will be paid to the complexities of contemporary art and cultural practices. The course will examine both practice and relevant theoretical paradigms.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE216
courses.notes: • Art history course.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Survey of Greek Art and Architecture
courses.description: A survey of Greek art and architecture from the earliest times to the coming of the Romans. Material studied may include the art of the Bronze Age, the development of Greek sculpture, the evolution of the Acropolis at Athens, and the change in art and architecture after Alexander the Great.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE241

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Survey of Roman Art and Architecture
courses.description: A survey of Roman art and architecture from the earliest times to the age of Constantine the Great. Material studied may include the art of the Etruscans, the evolution of Roman portraiture, innovations in architectural materials and forms, the use of art and architecture by the Emperors, and the change to Late Antique art.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE242

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: History of Visual Media to 1910
courses.description: This course provides a chronological and thematic overview of the history of visual media examining technologies such as the printing press, photography, early cinema, and the representation of perspective.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE244

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: History of Film and Visual Media from 1900 to Today
courses.description: The course provides a chronological and thematic overview of the history of visual media in Modernity and Postmodernity. It starts at the beginning of the 20th century with the rise of cinema and ends with discussion of the digital age.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE245

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Religion in Popular Film
courses.description: This course examines how religion has been a central concern and inspiration for filmmakers and how popular films have informed and shaped our understanding of religion.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE252, RS270R
courses.notes: • Film studies course.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Experimental Film
courses.description: The course introduces students to the history, methodologies, theories, and aesthetics of non-narrative experimental film with a focus on intersections between film and visual and performing arts.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE256

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Video, New Media and the Digital Turn
courses.description: This course analyzes the shift in visual practices of the 20th century transformed by the arrival of various digital technologies. An emphasis is placed on the increasing interdisciplinarity of new media, as well as their multi-sensory nature.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE257

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Global Queer Cinema
courses.description: This course introduces the varied production of world-wide gay, lesbian, bisexual, and transgender cinema. Inquiry will focus on how queer cinematic production serves as a vehicle for documentation and education, aesthetic and sexual experimentation, as well as cultural export and self-inquiry.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE 262

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Calligraphy to Conceptual Art: Text as an Image in Islamic and East Asian Visual Arts
courses.description: Exploring the history of Islamic and East Asian calligraphic arts and the study of Eastern and Western artists, this course examines multiple ways in which writing and other forms of visible language are incorporated into visual arts. Through studio projects, students explore conceptual approaches to text-based image making.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Art and Gender
courses.description: A study of selected themes dealing with gender in the history of art: e.g., the representation of the human body; portrayal of mythological, spiritual, and allegorical figures; professional and amateur artists and their status within societies; etc.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE281
courses.notes: • Art history course.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Canadian Art from the 17th Century to 1940
courses.description: This course examines art in Canada from the beginning of the European settlement in the 17th century to the Group of Seven and the Canadian Group of Painters. Some of the issues that will be investigated include the perception of Canada from abroad, the "new world", nation and nationhood, and the invention and appropriation of culture.
antireqText: Not completed any of the following: FINE282
courses.notes: • Art history course.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Fine Arts Abroad
courses.description: This is a topics course that provides students with an introduction to and a familiarity with the art and culture of a particular destination. Working in the field with landscape, cityscape, and monuments of art, students will employ a variety of media to develop techniques for visual reportage, documentation, note-taking, and journal-keeping. Individual aesthetic responses to a wide range of subject matter will be encouraged.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Visual Culture in Theory
courses.description: An advanced introduction to theorizing in art and media, highlighting the distinctive role of visual representation in cultural experience and the varied modes of thinking about images that visual representation has engendered. Readings will be drawn from several disciplines including art history, film and literary studies, media studies, and philosophy.

courses.subject: VCULT

courses.title: Topics Course in Museums, Galleries, Curatorship

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Philosophy of Art
courses.description: What is art? What is beauty? What do the two have to do with each other? This course introduces students to some fundamental issues in the philosophy of art, and to a variety of philosophical views on these issues.

courses.subject: VCULT
courses.title: Advanced Studies in Greek Art and Architecture
courses.description: An advanced survey of the art and architecture from a selected time period of Greek history. Material studied may include the art and architecture of the Aegean Bronze Age, and the Archaic, Classical, and Hellenistic periods. Archaeological, historical, and cultural issues specific to each time period will be discussed through the important media of the day.

courses.subject: VCULT

Archaeological, historical, and cultural issues specific to each time period will be discussed through the important media of the day.

courses.title: Religion in Science Fiction Films and Television
courses.description: This course examines how religion, religious themes, and the religious imagination are explored in and through science fiction film and television.
